protocol.source_plan: ../Systematic Literature Review Plan for Data Quality in Recommender Systems Using ISO_IEC 5259.pdf
protocol.objective: Identify, classify and appraise data-quality measurements in recommender systems, their operationalisation, validation, consequences and justified ISO/IEC 5259-2 correspondence.
protocol.scope: Any recommender paradigm; interaction, user, item/content, exposure, contextual, temporal, evaluation and synthetic/augmented data. The data property must itself be measured, manipulated, diagnosed or empirically assessed. Data-quality assessment can stand alone; downstream improvement and explicit ISO terminology are not required.

criteria.recommender_context: Trains, evaluates, operates or analyses a recommendation task; recommendation cannot be incidental.
criteria.data_quality_construct: Investigates a property of recommender data; incidental sparsity/noise descriptions are insufficient.
criteria.operational_evidence: Provides a procedure, measure, controlled manipulation or empirical data-quality assessment.
criteria.eligible_data_object: Interaction, profile, item/content, exposure, context, temporal, evaluation, synthetic or other task-relevant recommender data; algorithm architecture or output metrics alone are insufficient.
criteria.primary_research: Primary empirical or methodological research, including original evidence in mixed studies. Surveys/tutorials/editorials are secondary literature. Substantive workshop reports may qualify; preprints remain flagged provisional.

protocol.publication_policy: Journal/conference and substantive workshop primary studies; preprints provisional pending published-version linkage.

research_questions.RQ1: Which data objects and data-quality conditions have been empirically investigated?
research_questions.RQ2: How are conditions defined and measured, against which references and requirements?
research_questions.RQ3: What validation and reliability evidence supports the measures?
research_questions.RQ4: Which ISO/IEC 5259-2 correspondences are justified, and with what uncertainty?
research_questions.RQ5: How do measured conditions and interventions relate to recommender outcomes?
research_questions.RQ6: Which contexts moderate the relationships and where are measurement gaps?
